items.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021
items.q: you know Duke Ellington because of the way they sound and articulate notes and stuff.

ctx.x: Was it difficult to fit into the band or at that point was it sort of like a big band and Sun Ra had parts for everyone?

Sun Ra had parts for everything, and every day new parts. Every day he had something new. And he’d change what he’s got and the song, he’d change the stuff every day. He was amazing how he could do that, write the music like you’d write a letter. And he had so much music that the musicians couldn’t keep up there was so many things. So I said boy, and I didn’t understand none of that stuff in one sense because I was all thinking I know. And when I got with Sun Ra he just broke — tore that stuff away, that ego was…
